questions.question: Explain different types of solar cookers. Write about the advantages / and disadvantages of solar cooking.
questions.solution_html:
• Types – (4 marks)
  •  Box Cookers (Solar Box Ovens)
  •  Parabolic Cookers
  •  Panel Cookers
  •  Solar Ovens
  • Advantages of Solar Cooking (Any 3 points.(1 mark) each)
  • Environmentally Friendly
  •  No harmful emissions, reducing pollution.
  •  Does not rely on non-renewable resources like fossil fuels.
  • Sustainable
  •  Solar energy is free and inexhaustible, making solar cooking a long-term, renewable
  • energy source.
  • Cost-Effective
  •  After the initial setup, solar cookers incur no additional costs as they do not require fuel
  • or electricity
  • Health Benefits
  •  Cooks food at lower temperatures, preserving more nutrients compared to traditional
  • cooking methods.
  •  No harmful fumes or smoke, which makes it safer for health.
  • No Fuel Dependency
  •  Does not rely on gas, electricity, or firewood, which is particularly beneficial in areas
  • with limited access to these resources.
  • Disadvantages of Solar Cooking (Any 3 points.(1 mark) each)
  • Weather Dependency
  •  Solar cooking is only effective on sunny days. It doesn’t work well on cloudy, rainy, or
  • overcast days.
  •  Slow Cooking Time
  •  Solar cookers generally cook food more slowly than traditional cooking methods, which
  • may not be ideal when time is limited.
  • Limited Capacity
  •  Many solar cookers can only handle small quantities of food at a time, making them less
  • suitable for large meals.
  • Requires Space
  •  Some solar cookers, especially larger models, require more space for setup and
  • operation.
  • Initial Cost
  •  The cost of purchasing or building a solar cooker may be a barrier in some areas
  • although it’s often offset by the long-term savings on fuel.
questions.final_answer: although it’s often offset by the long-term savings on fuel

questions.question: Describe on microwave cooking.
questions.solution_html:
•  Microwave cooking is a method of cooking food using electromagnetic waves from a power
  • source magnetron.
  •  It works on dielectric heating, where polar molecules (mainly water) vibrate rapidly when
  • exposed to microwaves, producing heat.
  •  Heat is produced inside the food, unlike conventional cooking where heat moves from outside to
  • inside.
  •  The efficiency of microwave cookery depends upon the constituents of food being cooked.
  •  Water in food converts microwaves to heat energy very efficiently followed by starch, cellulose
  • and protein. Least effective is fatty tissues.
  •  Only microwave-safe materials like glass, ceramic, and certain plastics can be used; metals reflect
  • microwaves.((1 mark) for each point)
  •  Any 2 advantages of microwave cooking ((1 mark) for each point)
  •  Any 2disadvantages of microwave cooking ((1 mark) for each point)
questions.final_answer:  Any 2disadvantages of microwave cooking ( for each point)

questions.question: Describe on microwave cooking.

  • source magnetron.

  • exposed to microwaves, producing heat.
  •  Heat is produced inside the food, unlike conventional cooking where heat moves from outside to
  • inside.
  •  The efficiency of microwave cookery depends upon the constituents of food being cooked.
  •  Water in food converts microwaves to heat energy very efficiently followed by starch, cellulose
  • and protein. Least effective is fatty tissues.

  • microwaves.((1 mark) for each point)

questions.question: Describe standardisation, objectives and purpose.
questions.solution_html:
• Standardized Recipe ((2 marks))
  • A standardized recipe is one that has been tested multiple times and produces the same quality and yield under
  • the same conditions. For example, a recipe that always gives 10 servings of identical-tasting "Vegetable Pulao."
  • According to USDA, it is a recipe that consistently gives the same results in quality and quantity after repeated
  • trials. For example, a soup recipe that always yields 2 liters with the same taste. Recipe standardization is the
  • process of fixing ingredients, measurements, methods, and portion sizes to ensure consistency. For example
  • using exactly 200 g rice and 500 ml water each time.
  • OBJECTIVES ((3 marks))
